tools.name: ae_get_state
tools.title: After Effects state
tools.description: Where After Effects is right now: app version, the open project (path, unsaved changes, item count), the active comp (id, size, fps, duration, work area, current time, layer count), the selected project items and layers, and the render queue. Call it first, and again whenever the user may have changed something by hand. Read-only and cheap.

tools.name: ae_list_items
tools.title: List project items
tools.description: Project panel items: comps, footage, solids, placeholders and folders with id, name, type, size, duration, fps, file path and parent folder. Use it to find the item id that ae_add_layer, ae_get_comp or ae_render need. Read-only.

name_contains.description: Only items whose name contains this text (case-insensitive)

limit.description: Maximum items returned (the receipt says when it truncated)

tools.name: ae_get_comp
tools.title: Inspect comp
tools.description: One comp in depth: settings (size, fps, duration, background, work area, motion blur, frame blending), comp markers and every layer with id, index, name, type, source, timing (start/in/out/stretch), parent, switches, blend mode, track matte, effects and the paths of its animated properties. Default: the active comp. Read-only.

comp.description: Comp id (`comp_id`) or exact name; default: the active comp

tools.name: ae_get_layer
tools.title: Inspect layer
tools.description: Deep view of one layer: transform values at `time`, every keyframe of its animated properties (time, value, interpolation, temporal ease), effects with their parameters, the text document of text layers, masks and expressions (with errors). Use it before changing animation so you edit what is there. Read-only.

comp.description: Comp id (`comp_id`) or exact name; default: the active comp

anyOf.description: Layer id (`layer_id` from ae_get_comp or a receipt; After Effects 2022+)

layer.description: Layer: its id (`layer_id`), {"index": n} (1 = top) or exact name

time.description: Comp time for the transform values (default: the comp's current time)

tools.name: ae_capture_frame
tools.title: Capture comp frame
tools.description: Render one comp frame to a PNG and return it as an image: your eyes. After any visual change capture the moments that matter (first frame, each entrance end, mid-hold, last frame) and critique them against the taste guide: text inside title-safe and readable, one focal point, nothing ending abruptly. Wide comps are downsampled to `max_width` through the comp's resolution factor, which is restored afterwards. Read-only.

comp.description: Comp id (`comp_id`) or exact name; default: the active comp

time.description: Comp time in seconds (default: the comp's current time); snapped to the frame grid

Solids default to the comp size in ink #0B0B0F; shapes to a centred 30 % rect filled with accent #FF5A36. Text has its own tool (ae_add_text).

tools.name: ae_add_text
tools.title: Add text
tools.description: Add a text layer that already looks designed. `style` picks the TASTE type scale at 1080p (scaled by the comp's short side): headline 96 px bold, title 72 px bold, subtitle 44 px, lower-third 54 px name (+ 34 px role via `subtitle`), caption 42 px. Fonts fall back Inter > SF Pro Display > Helvetica Neue > Arial. Tracking -15 on headlines, +80 on ALL CAPS; leading 1.1x headlines / 1.3x body. `placement` keeps the text inside title-safe (10 % inset; 9:16 also avoids the top 12 % and bottom 20 %); lower-third sits left at title-safe with its baseline at 80 % (70 % vertical). Lines over 32 characters are broken at balanced word boundaries, too-wide text is scaled down to fit, and a soft shadow is added over footage. Optional `animation` applies a motion preset at the layer's start.

tools.name: ae_animate
tools.title: Animate property
tools.description: Keyframe a property with real eased keyframes. Each segment eases with the TASTE curves (default smooth; out/entrance for arrivals, in/exit for departures, in-out between resting states, snap for punchy pops, linear only for opacity crossfades, loops and tickers, hold for steps) or a custom {x1, y1, x2, y2}, mapped exactly to After Effects speed/influence per dimension (spatial properties along the path). Existing keyframes inside the new time span are replaced (all of them with `replace`). `overshoot` (0-0.06) adds an editable settle keyframe for playful brands only.

tools.name: ae_apply_motion_preset
tools.title: Apply motion preset
tools.description: Tasteful, editable animation on a layer. fade-in / fade-out (opacity), slide-in / slide-out (4 % of the frame width with opacity), scale-pop (92 % to 100 %), blur-in, whip-in (a fast push with motion blur), ken-burns (slow scale + pan over the shot, in-out), push-in (100 % to 104 % over the shot), drift (a slow procedural float, an expression); text only: typewriter, word-cascade, line-rise (text animators with a Range Selector, so a human can retime them). Defaults: entrances 0.6 s eased out, exits 0.4 s eased in, pops 0.27 s snap, stagger 0.06 s per word / 0.12 s per line; entrances start at the layer's in point, exits end at its out point. `intensity` 0-1 (0.5 = the TASTE default) scales distance, scale or blur within the TASTE range. Keyframes already in the preset's time range on the same properties are replaced.

tools.name: ae_render_for_zenvi
tools.title: Render for Zenvi
tools.description: Render a comp (default: the active comp) for a Zenvi linked clip and return everything Zenvi needs: path, comp id and name, project, size, fps, duration and a ready `link` object (SPEC 3.6) for the desktop's import_linked_media_tool. alpha: true renders ProRes 4444 with alpha (for overlays over other clips; QuickTime Animation where there is no ProRes 4444 template), else H.264 (before After Effects 2023: ProRes 4444, then QuickTime Animation). Only codecs Zenvi links: h264, prores4444, qtrle. Blocks After Effects while it renders; the render queue item is removed afterwards.
